text:
incident-bot: [PD] High-severity: GPU host node-67 (gcp-us-west1) rebooted unexpectedly. Multiple serving tasks evicted. Alert: node_health.rebooted (count=1)

alice: Paging oncall. I’m on it — switching to incident channel. Any customer impact reported?

mika: Seeing surge in 500s from api-redwood-gen in US-WEST-1 from 11:20 -> 11:24. ~2% error rate spike, latency +300ms p50. I'll open a customer-impact note.

alice: Thanks. First step: cordon node-67 and drain. Which pods were affected?

ben: Runtime shows 6 inference workers evicted, 2 heavy-embed jobs hit OOM on their container-level. I ran: `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-67 -o wide` — will paste list.

ben: ```
pod/api-gen-5f6d7   Running   0/3     Node: node-67
pod/embed-heavy-2    Evicted   0/1     Node: node-67
pod/worker-cache-1   CrashLoop  1/1     Node: node-67
```

carla: Noted. Can someone fetch kernel logs and dmesg from the node before we reprovision? Might be PCIe AER / ECC.

alice: Copy. ben, can you ssh the host and collect /var/log/kern.log, /var/log/syslog, and output of `dmesg --ctime`? Also get nvidia-smi -q and `journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager --since "15 minutes ago"`.

ben: On it. Pasting key snippets:

ben: ```
[Nov 03 11:19:52] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[Nov 03 11:19:53] pci 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: status=0x00000001
[Nov 03 11:19:54] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Multiple Err: First
[Nov 03 11:19:55] kernel: Hardware ECC detected, corrected error on memory device 3
[Nov 03 11:19:56] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: GPU watchdog timeout
```

carla: That looks like PCIe AER then GPU kernel panic. Could be host-level PCIe instability or noisy neighbor causing bus resets. Any recent firmware updates or noisy VMs?

nate: I saw a large throughput burst to that host starting 11:18 from one tenant (tenant-id t-83a). Could be a single large batch job blasting the PCIe. I've flagged their tasks in telemetry.

mika: Customer-impact: api-gen error trace shows 503s during exact window. I'm drafting a status update: minimal customer impact but degraded latency.

alice: Mitigation steps executed: node cordoned, pods drained to other nodes (some failed due to GPU capacity). We've reprovisioned a replacement node-92 to pick up reserved workloads. Rate limiter added to embeddings queue to throttle big batches.

carla: Good. For RCA we need: full dmesg, nv-hostengine logs, PCIe AER counters pre/post, any GPU ECC counts from `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`. Upload to ops bucket with incident id INC-193900. Link: https://ops.redwood/internal/INC-193900/artifacts (uploader in progress).

ben: Uploaded kern.log and dmesg excerpts to the link. Also pushed `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` output. Key ECC counters: Device 0 corrected ECC errors increased from 0 -> 124 in 30s.

carla: 124 corrected ECC errors in 30s is concerning. Hypothesis A: transient PCIe link error caused GPU to drop off bus, subsequent ECC noise led to kernel watchdog. Hypothesis B: GPU hardware degradation (thermal or memory DIMM) causing ECC spikes. Hypothesis C: Noisy neighbor VM causing high PCIe traffic and bus instability.

alice: Which hypothesis is most likely given AER + corrected ECC + Xid 79? My money is Hypothesis A (PCIe errors). But we should verify link-level CRC counters from NIC/switch if possible and ask GCP to check host firmware/BIOS.

gcp-support: Thanks for the data. We see repeated AER events on that host. We're initiating host-level diagnostics and will check for recent firmware or BIOS updates. We might reprovision to new hardware if we find persistent AER. We'll update within 2 hours.

nate: For the tenant burst: throttled their batch window and contacted the tenant owner. Also added temporary autoscale headroom in the cluster to avoid pod evictions when we drain nodes.

mika: Sent customer update: "We experienced a brief GPU host reboot in us-west1 affecting a subset of inference requests between 11:19-11:24. We mitigated by shifting workloads and adding throttles. We're investigating root cause; no data exfiltration or data loss reported."

carla: Next steps for RCA: (1) correlate GPU ECC counts with PCIe AER timestamps (ben), (2) request GCP host diag & firmware check (alice), (3) run synthetic GPU memory test on replacement host to reproduce ECC (carla), (4) review tenant batch limits and autoscale buffers (nate).

ben: I correlated event timestamps: ECC spike aligns with AER and Xid 79. Attached table in artifacts.

alice: For mitigation going forward: add stricter per-tenant batch concurrency caps, automatic soft-cordon on repeated AER events (temp), and playbook entry for evacuating GPU nodes when ECC>100 within 1 minute. Will create PR for autoscaler config.

mika: I'll prepare the post-incident note once we have GCP's findings. For now status: mitigated, partial customer impact documented.

gcp-support: Quick update: host firmware last updated 6 months ago; diagnostics show degraded PCIe slot signal on node-67. We're recommending host replacement and moving the VM to a different host.

carla: OK, risk reduced. We'll mark the node as retired and not reprovision same host id. Linking to infra ticket INFRA-721.

alice: Handoff — I'm going offline for dinner in 10m. Carla, can you take lead on RCA artifacts and follow up with GCP for final report? Ben, please add the ECC/Xid correlation to the incident doc. Mika, finalize customer-facing timeline. Nate, keep an eye on tenant throttling changes.

carla: Taking lead. I'll post a follow-up summary in this thread when the GCP final report is in.

ben: Added correlation CSV and a short script to parse `dmesg` for AER/Xid/ECC events to the artifacts. Command: `grep -E "AER|Xid|ECC|NVRM" kern.log > aer-xid-ecc.log`

mika: Thx — closing on-call loop. Will update postmortem channel once RCA draft done. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-193900 marked mitigated by alice at 11:36. Remaining action items recorded in INFRA-721 and INC-193900 postmortem.
